basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 22.' and it opens 'Vers. 22. Postquam biberunt cameli. Quod Rebecca non solum viro dedit potum, verum etiam'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 22. Postquam biberunt cameli. Quod Rebecca non solum viro dedit potum, verum etiam camelos adaquavit, significat quia Ecclesia nulli debet subtrahere verbum praedicationis, sed sapientibus et stultis in commune annuntiare. Hinc Paulus dicit: Graecis | et barbaris, sapientibus et insipientibus debitor sum (Rom. L, 14). Vel aliter. Per camelos carnem nostram debemus accipere. Cameli ergo adaquantur, quando cura corporis agitur, non tamen in desideriis, sed in necessitate, ut Rebecca sive anima gestare possit.
